svg.aria-label: A Go compile error repeated across five identical runs survives compression, while the lines around it are dropped; when nothing survives, bilro says so instead of printing an empty screen.
svg.text: a line reporting a failure is never dropped

g.text: run 1 — nothing learned yet
compiling module cache
resolving dependencies
./main.go:10:2: undefined: fooBar
build finished with errors
Everything is new. Nothing is dropped.
run 5 — the same output, four times over
compiling module cache
resolving dependencies
./main.go:10:2: undefined: fooBar
build finished with errors
The error repeats in every run, exactly like the noise around it —
and it stays. Not one word of it matches a failure keyword;
it is recognised by the shape every compiler prints: path, line, column.
when nothing survives
identical to what this command has printed before:
40 lines suppressed. bilro saw no failure among them,
but it only recognises the ones it can name —
run without bilro if the result matters.
An empty screen reads as "the command printed nothing".
And absence of failure is not provable from a list of words,
so it does not claim it.
